## PLM, the van Leer harmonic-mean slope (`type: plm`) {#sec-ch04-plm}

### Summary

PLM fits a straight line through each cell and reads the two face states off its ends. The slope of the line is
the harmonic mean of the differences to the two neighbours. That choice makes the slope zero at a local maximum
or minimum and never steeper than twice the smaller difference, so a face value cannot overshoot its neighbours.
The scheme is second order where the field is smooth and first order at extrema. It is selected by
`type: plm` and is off by default. Positive cells therefore give positive face values, but the limiter
guarantees nothing for the updated density or pressure. snapy guarantees no positivity of either; it has floors,
the equation-of-state limiter and a redo (@sec-ch08, @sec-ch08-eoslimiter, @sec-ch08-redo).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Face states $\bar q_i \mp \tfrac12 D_i$ with the harmonic-mean slope $D_i$ of @eq-ch04-plm-slope.

**Data.** Reads three cell values per cell; writes the two face states of each cell.

**Placement.** Inside the reconstruction of each direction (@sec-ch04-framework), every stage.

**Activation.** `type: plm`; default off. `scale` is read and has no effect.

**Guarantee / limits.** Face values stay between neighbours; second order smooth, first order at extrema.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch04-plm-tests; `test_plm.release`, `derivation_check.py` `[C3]`, `recon_check.py` `[C5]`.
:::

Local symbols: $D_- = \bar q_i - \bar q_{i-1}$ and $D_+ = \bar q_{i+1} - \bar q_i$ the
one-sided differences of cell $i$; $D_i$ its limited slope (all in the units of $q$, per cell); $a_0, a_1, \dots$ the Taylor
coefficients of @sec-ch04-dc; $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=2^{-52}$ machine epsilon (appendix A, notation group 7).

### Derivation

#### The slope

The code computes

$$
D_i = \begin{cases}
\dfrac{2\,D_-D_+}{D_- + D_+} & D_-D_+ > 0,\\[2mm]
0 & \text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
\qquad q^{\mathrm R}_i = \bar q_i - \tfrac12 D_i,\quad q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1} = \bar q_i + \tfrac12 D_i .
$$ {#eq-ch04-plm-slope}

#### Why a face value never leaves the range of its neighbours In the code, @eq-ch04-plm-slope is `dwm`, `wlv` and `wrv` ({{< code src/recon/plm.cpp PLMInterpImpl::forward >}}).

1. *At an extremum the slope is zero.* An extremum is exactly $D_-D_+\le0$, so both face values equal
   $\bar q_i$[^rg-6b1b6007ca8d].
2. *Otherwise $D_-$ and $D_+$ have one sign*; take both positive (the negative case is the mirror image).
3. *The slope is at most twice either difference.* $2D_+ - D_i = 2D_+^2/(D_- + D_+) \ge 0$ and
   $2D_- - D_i = 2D_-^2/(D_- + D_+)\ge0$; `derivation_check.py` `[C3]` simplifies both with sympy.
4. *Hence* $0 \le \tfrac12D_i \le D_+$, so $q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1} = \bar q_i + \tfrac12D_i \in [\bar q_i, \bar q_{i+1}]$,
   and likewise $q^{\mathrm R}_i \in [\bar q_{i-1}, \bar q_i]$. No new extremum is created at a face, which is the
   total-variation-diminishing property; `recon_check.py` `[C5]` finds no violation on 20 000 random triples.

#### Why it is second order on a smooth field

1. *The two differences of cell averages.* With the Taylor coefficients of @sec-ch04-dc,
   $D_\mp = a_1h \mp a_2h^2 + O(h^3)$.
2. *Their harmonic mean.* $2D_-D_+/(D_-+D_+) = a_1h + \bigl(\tfrac54a_1a_3 - a_2^2\bigr)h^3/a_1 + O(h^4)$: the
   centred slope to $O(h^3)$ wherever $a_1 \ne 0$.
3. *The face value.* $\bar q_i + \tfrac12D_i - u(x_{i+1/2}) = -\tfrac{a_2}{6}h^2 + O(h^3)$: second order.
   `derivation_check.py` `[C3]` derives both coefficients with sympy.
4. *At an extremum* $a_1 = 0$, step 2 no longer holds, the slope is clipped to zero, and the face value is
   first order as in @eq-ch04-dc-error.

#### Round-off: why the slope is finite and how far a face value can stray

1. *No division by zero.* The quotient is taken only where $D_-D_+ > 0$; then $D_-$ and $D_+$ have one sign and
   $\lvert D_- + D_+\rvert \ge \max(\lvert D_-\rvert, \lvert D_+\rvert) > 0$. A small additive guard could not do
   this: for $D_\pm$ near the smallest normal single-precision number, $10^{-38}$, the guard itself would be
   rounded away and the quotient would be $0/0$. `test_plm.release` feeds exactly such stencils
   (`interp_plm_round_off_slopes_stay_finite`).
2. *Count the roundings.* Each difference is one rounding, the product one more, the sum one, the quotient one:
   with $\lvert\eta\rvert\le\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$ per operation, the computed slope is $D_i(1+\eta_D)$ with
   $\lvert\eta_D\rvert \le 6(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2) = 3\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ to first order (two from the product's inputs plus one, one from
   the sum's inputs plus one, one from the quotient).
3. *The face value* adds one rounding: $\lvert\hat q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1} - q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1}\rvert \le
   (\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)\lvert q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1}\rvert + (\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)\cdot3\lvert D_i\rvert$, and by step 3 of the
   bound above $\lvert D_i\rvert\le 2\min(\lvert D_-\rvert, \lvert D_+\rvert)$. So a face value can leave
   $[\bar q_i, \bar q_{i+1}]$ by at most $(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)\lvert q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1}\rvert +
   3\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\min(\lvert D_-\rvert, \lvert D_+\rvert)$, about $10^{-15}$ of the local value in double.

### Numerical method

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-plm-slope
#| fig-cap: "The PLM slope. (a) The line PLM fits in each cell (green) through the cell values (sky-blue circles) of a smooth profile with a kink; at the extrema (vermillion squares) the slope is zero and the cell is flat. (b) The harmonic-mean slope as a function of the ratio of the two one-sided differences (green), the bound $2\\min(1, D_+/D_-)$ that keeps the face values between the neighbours (vermillion, dashed), and the unlimited centred slope (blue, dotted)."
#| fig-alt: "Left: dots with short green line segments through them, flat at four boxed extrema. Right: a green curve rising from zero at ratio zero and staying below a dashed bound, with a dotted straight line for comparison."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch04.figures.fig_ch04_schemes import make_plm
make_plm()
```

**Stencil and ghosts.** Three cells: `stencils()` is 3, so the framework needs two ghost cells.

**Where it is used.** `PLMInterpImpl::forward` overrides the base class and returns both face states in one
pass; `left` and `right` of the base class call it.

### Code

**A minimal input.**

```yaml
dynamics:
  reconstruct:
    vertical:   {type: plm}
    horizontal: {type: plm}
```

**What the parser accepts and refuses.** The framework's rules apply (@sec-ch04-framework). PLM has no limiter
option: the harmonic mean is hard-coded, and a key such as `limiter` is refused by the reconstruct parser.

**The excerpt.** `PLMInterpImpl::forward` ({{< code src/recon/plm.cpp PLMInterpImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  auto dw = w.narrow(dim, 1, size - 1) - w.narrow(dim, 0, size - 1);
  auto dwl = dw.narrow(dim, 0, size - 2);
  auto dwr = dw.narrow(dim, 1, size - 2);
  auto dw2 = dwl * dwr;
  // dw2 > 0 keeps dwl + dwr away from zero; an epsilon cannot (0/0 at 1e-38)
  auto dwm =
      torch::where(dw2 > 0, 2. * dw2 / (dwl + dwr), torch::zeros_like(dw2));

  wlv.copy_(w.narrow(dim, 1, size - 2) - 0.5 * dwm);
  wrv.copy_(w.narrow(dim, 1, size - 2) + 0.5 * dwm);
```

`dwl` and `dwr` are $D_-$ and $D_+$; `dwm` is $D_i$ of @eq-ch04-plm-slope with the branch written as a product;
`wlv` and `wrv` are $q^{\mathrm R}_i$ and $q^{\mathrm L}_{i+1}$.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the slope and face values | {{< code src/recon/plm.cpp PLMInterpImpl::forward >}} | `dwm` | `type: plm` |
| stencil width | {{< code src/recon/interpolation.hpp PLMInterpImpl >}} | `stencils` | 3 |
| registration | {{< code src/recon/interpolation.cpp InterpImpl::create >}} | `PLMInterp` | |

20 000 random triples and a face value equal to the cell value at every extremum.[^plm-run] `test_plm.release`
passes at the pin on CPU, one rank (@tbl-ch04-ctest-run). No test measures the order of PLM on a refinement
ladder.

### Limits

1. **One limiter.** The harmonic mean is the only slope; `interp_simple.hpp` also defines `minmod`, `superbee`,
   `vanleer` and an MC limiter, which no production path calls.
2. **Uniform-grid slope.** @eq-ch04-plm-slope takes raw differences, so it is the limited slope of the underlying
   linear fit only on equal widths. A deck that *declares* a stretched $x_1$ cannot reach that state: `plm` has no
   per-face $x_1$ route and setup refuses it there, as it refuses every interpolant but `weno5` and `cp5`
   ({{< code src/recon/interpolation.hpp InterpImpl::set_x1_coeffs >}}; @sec-ch04-x1volume). The slope is still the
   raw-difference one on $x_2$ and $x_3$, and on an undeclared non-uniform grid.
3. **No measured order.** Second order away from extrema is derived (steps 1 to 3) and not measured on a ladder.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-6b1b6007ca8d]: $\bar q_i$ — the cell average stored by the code, written with the bar only where a point value of the same quantity also appears. The overbar means the cell average and nothing else: a midpoint, a reference or a background value never carries a bar; notation only; see @sec-appa
